subject: religious-studies

moments.title: Sermon on the Mount
moments.body: Matthew's Gospel (chapters 5-7) records Jesus's longest single block of ethical teaching. Beatitudes ('Blessed are the poor in spirit...'), the antitheses ('You have heard that it was said... But I say to you...'), the Lord's Prayer, teaching on judgment, anxiety, possessions. Luke's Sermon on the Plain (Luke 6) is a parallel.
moments.takeaway: Whether Matthew 5-7 is one historical sermon or a composed collection of teachings, it functions as the heart of Christian ethical teaching.

moments.title: Augustine's interpretation
moments.who: Augustine, 'On the Sermon on the Mount'
moments.body: Augustine (in 'De Sermone Domini in Monte', c. 393-396) treats the Sermon as a complete summary of Christian moral life. The interpretive frame — Sermon as Christian ethics — has dominated subsequently.
moments.takeaway: The Sermon's centrality is a patristic decision as much as a feature of the text. Other gospel sections could have been similarly canonised.

moments.title: Bonhoeffer and 'cheap grace'
moments.body: Bonhoeffer's reading: the Sermon is not impossible idealism but the actual calling of the disciple. 'Cheap grace' — forgiveness without repentance, salvation without commitment — is the enemy. The Sermon demands what it demands.

quote.text: When Christ calls a man, he bids him come and die.
quote.attrib: Dietrich Bonhoeffer, The Cost of Discipleship, 1937

moments.takeaway: Bonhoeffer was executed by the Nazis in 1945. His own life embodied his exegesis.

now.title: Living the Sermon
now.body: The Sermon continues to be central — to Christian preaching, to Tolstoy's pacifism, to Gandhi's non-violence (he read it constantly), to Martin Luther King's strategy, to monastic and lay Christian movements. Anabaptist and pacifist traditions read it as binding; mainline traditions interpret it variously.
now.open_questions: Was Jesus a literal pacifist? Mennonites, Quakers and some Catholics say yes; others see hyperbolic teaching that doesn't preclude just war. The exegetical question continues.

reflection: A series of teachings recorded by one early Christian community has become one of the most influential ethical texts in world history. Its actual content — radical love of enemies, indifference to possessions, focus on the kingdom — continues to challenge readers in every generation.
